Only methods declared in sugar-gallery/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\Gallery

AnsiGuard final class

The one place that decides which escape sequences a widget will echo verbatim.

MethodSummary
static assertSafe(string $ansi): stringReturn $ansi untouched when it carries nothing but SGR styling and printable text; throw when it carries anything else.
static isSafe(string $ansi): boolWhether assertSafe() would accept $ansi.
static sanitize(string $ansi): stringDrop every unsafe run from $ansi, keeping its SGR styling and text.
static stripControls(string $text): stringReduce $text to what a *plain* (unstyled) title may contain: keep the text runs and drop every escape the scanner sees, SGR included.
static stripSentinels(string $text): stringRemove the candy-mouse zone sentinels U+E000/U+E001 — and nothing else — as the lib's public seam for the fleet's untrusted-for-marked-frames law (gallery review M8/m19). Anything the app hands to a zone-marking \SugarCraft\Mouse\Zones\Manager must have passed this sweep first: a forged sentinel pair inside marked bytes is markup to the scanner downstream, so a fresh-id pair mints a phantom hit-testable zone and a duplicate-id pair poisons the app's click path (denial of service). Delegates to sugar-core's Sanitize::stripZoneSentinels(); legitimate ImageOverlay markers (U+E002 and up) and all other private-use glyphs survive untouched.

CardSize final readonly class

One size vocabulary for a poster card: width, poster rows and the two gutters, clamped ONCE at ingress with the same floors the loose-int seams always applied (width ≥ 4, height ≥ 1, spacings ≥ 0). Accepted additively wherever the library took those ints — PosterGrid::new(), PosterGrid::withCardSize(), Rail::render(), Rail::perRow(), Rail::frameHeight(), PosterCard::render() — and the int signatures stay byte-identical.

MethodSummary
static new(int $width, int $height, int $hSpacing = 2, int $vSpacing = 1): self
static from(int|self $width, ?int $height = null, ?int $hSpacing = null, ?int $vSpacing = null): selfNormalise an int|CardSize seam: a CardSize passes through untouched (its own gutters win), an int width needs its poster height.
width(): intCard width in cells (clamped ≥ 4).
height(): intPoster rows per card (clamped ≥ 1).
hSpacing(): intHorizontal gutter (clamped ≥ 0).
vSpacing(): intVertical gutter (clamped ≥ 0).
withWidth(int $width): self
withHeight(int $height): self
withHSpacing(int $hSpacing): self
withVSpacing(int $vSpacing): self

Lang final class

Per-library translation facade for sugar-gallery.

PosterCard final readonly class

One poster tile: a poster area (a placeholder until its rendered ANSI is attached), a title, and an optional progress bar (e.g. continue-watching).

MethodSummary
__construct(public string $id, public string $title, public ?string $posterUrl = null, public ?float $progress = null, public ?string $poster = null, public ?string $styledTitle = null, public ?string $posterImage = null, public ?int $imageId = null, public bool $failed = false, string $posterHash = '')
static new(string $id, string $title, ?string $posterUrl = null, ?float $progress = null, ?string $poster = null, ?string $styledTitle = null, ?string $posterImage = null, ?int $imageId = null, bool $failed = false): selfCanonical factory — mirrors the public constructor.
withFailed(bool $failed = true): selfMark the cell's art-fetch as failed (or, passing false, back to loading): the body shows a localised unavailable line over '?' fill rows instead of the loading skeleton, and hasPoster() reports the cell unfilled so a retry policy still re-queues it. Attaching real art afterwards (withPoster/withImage) does NOT clear the flag — pass withFailed(false) alongside the fill, which is exactly what a retry-resolved callback does.
withTitle(string $title): selfReturn a copy with a different plain title (sugar-gallery-010: the library shipped with* carriers for every other field but the host had to hand-spell the whole nine-argument constructor to rename a card). The styled title is a SEPARATE field — see withStyledTitle(); a card rendering a styled title keeps showing it until that one moves.
isFailed(): boolWhether the last fetch for this cell failed (see withFailed()).
withPoster(string $ansi): selfAttach already-rendered poster bytes VERBATIM. The caller owns their safety — see the class docblock's trust-boundary law and withSafePoster() for the coercing setter.
withSafePoster(string $ansi): selfAttach poster bytes after keeping only SGR styling and printable glyphs — the coercing setter at the poster trust boundary, for bytes that arrived from somewhere the caller cannot vouch for (a cache, a server, a disk pipeline). AnsiGuard::sanitize() drops cursor moves, erases, and every OSC/DCS/APC payload (forged OSC-8 hyperlinks and stray ESC bytes alike); a poster rendered by e.g. Mosaic::halfBlock() from clean art is returned byte-identical, because half-block glyphs and truecolour SGR are exactly what the guard admits.
withImage(string $bytes, int $id): selfAttach a pixel-graphics poster (sixel/kitty/iTerm2 bytes) to be painted as an overlay at $id. Unlike withPoster() the bytes never enter the text frame — the card renders a marker block reserving the poster area, and the \SugarCraft\Core\Program paints the image on top. The graphics bytes are stored VERBATIM and bypass the text guard — they are out-of-band payloads, not frame text: the CALLER owns their provenance. An $id outside ImageOverlay's paintable range degrades the cell to an unfilled skeleton (re-queued for a fresh id) instead of throwing.
withProgress(?float $progress): selfSet the download/watch progress fraction, or null to UNSET it (the progress row disappears). NAN/±INF are refused at this ingress (sugar-gallery-035: ±INF read silently as a full bar and NAN even rendered "100 %" downstream — a poisoned float from a remote ratio must name itself, not decorate the card).
withStyledTitle(string $ansi, bool $assertSafe = false): selfAttach a pre-styled (ANSI) title to display in place of the plain $title — e.g. a fuzzy-highlighted search result. The escapes are preserved and the title cell is padded to the correct visible width. The plain $title is kept for identity/sort.
withSafeStyledTitle(string $ansi): selfAttach a styled title after dropping everything that is not SGR styling (AnsiGuard::sanitize()) — the coercing setter of the withStyledTitle() trust boundary, for a highlight built over text the caller does not control. Colour may be lost; a cursor move never will be.
static assertSafeAnsi(string $ansi): stringGuard for the withStyledTitle() trust boundary: return $ansi when it carries nothing but SGR styling and printable text, throw otherwise.
hasPoster(): boolWhether this cell holds art the grid can paint — either inline cell text or an overlay fill. The fill policy keys on this, so it must agree with what render() actually draws: an overlay blob with no id has no marker to paint, renders as a skeleton, and must count as unfilled so the owner re-queues it.
render(bool $focused, int|CardSize $width, ?int $posterHeight = null): stringRender a fixed-width block: poster (or a placeholder) rows, a title row, and a progress row when set. Every row is exactly $width visual cells wide so a rail or grid can stitch cards side by side.
renderMemoKey(bool $focused, int|CardSize $width, ?int $posterHeight = null): ?stringA content key naming the exact bytes render() emits at this geometry, or null when the card is a failed cell (see bodyKey() — a locale-resolved notice line cannot be content-keyed without freezing a translation).
static clearFitCache(): intDrop the shared fitted-body memo, returning how many entries were cleared. Rendering populates it lazily and it is self-bounding (FIT_CACHE_CAP); a long-lived program that churns through many distinct posters can call this to reclaim the memory eagerly (e.g. on a result-set reset). Purely an optimization — clearing only costs the next render its fit work again and never changes a single output byte.

PosterGrid final class

A responsive, 2-D virtualized poster grid for large collections.

MethodSummary
static new(int|CardSize $cardWidth, ?int $posterHeight = null, int $hSpacing = 2, int $vSpacing = 1): selfA new empty grid laid out with the given card geometry. Feed it a viewport (withViewport()) and a result set (withReset() / withItems()).
cardSize(): CardSizeThe effective card geometry as one CardSize value.
cardWidth(): intEffective card width — the CLAMPED value construction promised (≥ 4). The clamp was invisible before these accessors existed (sugar-gallery-006): hosts had to re-derive it by hand to size a surrounding frame.
posterHeight(): intEffective poster rows per card (clamped ≥ 1).
hSpacing(): intEffective horizontal gutter (clamped ≥ 0).
vSpacing(): intEffective vertical gutter (clamped ≥ 0).
withCardSize(int|CardSize $cardWidth, ?int $posterHeight = null, ?int $hSpacing = null, ?int $vSpacing = null): selfRe-lay the card geometry mid-session (a resizable pane): the loaded items ride unchanged and the cursor re-enters range through the same synced() law the viewport verbs use (sugar-gallery-011: geometry was frozen at construction, forcing hosts to rebuild the grid and re-splice every cached card to resize it). Null spacing arguments keep the grid's current gutters.
withReset(int $total): selfBegin a fresh result set of $total items (e.g. after a filter/sort change): drops all cached cards and returns the cursor to the top.
withTotal(int $total): selfUpdate the known total without dropping cached cards (e.g. a first page revealed how many items exist), clamping the cursor into range.
static assertCardList(string $entryMethod, array $items): arrayThe shared card-map ingress law. A host-supplied card map must have int keys and PosterCard values, or it is refused AT ADMISSION naming the entry method (2026-11-03 fail-loud law; sugar-gallery-003: Rail ran its own unguarded copy of this shape, so a string key entered there and detonated later as a frame-wide TypeError inside render()).
withItems(array $items): selfSplice a page of cards in at their ABSOLUTE indices, merging with whatever is already loaded (new cards win). This is how a range fetch lands.
withItem(int $index, PosterCard $card): selfSet (or replace) a single card by absolute index — e.g. an async poster arriving.
withoutItemsOutside(array $range): selfEvict every loaded card whose absolute index falls OUTSIDE the inclusive [$start, $end] window, keeping the sparse $items map bounded to the live region. The map otherwise only ever grows — each range fetch accumulates cards forever, even after the user scrolls far past them — so an owner paging a very large library should prune off-screen cards after each move, typically passing a widened visibleRange() (a superset of what will be re-fetched). Returns the receiver unchanged when the window already covers every loaded card (nothing to evict), so a caller can cheaply detect the no-op by identity.
withViewport(int $cols, int $rows): selfResize the rendered area (cells), re-clamping the scroll to keep the cursor visible.
left(): self
right(): self
up(): self
down(): self
pageDown(): self
pageUp(): self
home(): self
end(): self
moveTo(int $index): selfJump the cursor to an absolute index (e.g. an A–Z letter offset), clamped.
visibleRange(int $overscanRows = 0): arrayThe inclusive absolute-index window currently on screen, optionally widened by $overscanRows above and below for prefetch. The owner compares this to what it last fetched and loads the covering page(s). Returns [0, -1] (an empty range) when there are no items.
needsFetch(?array $lastFetched, int $overscanRows = 0): boolWhether the current visibleRange() still needs a fetch given the last range the owner already loaded — the fetch-dedup companion to visibleRange(). Returns true when the visible window (widened by the same $overscanRows you page with) is NOT fully covered by $lastFetched, so an owner can skip the redundant range fetch while the cursor moves inside an already-loaded window:
visibleCards(int $overscanRows = 0): arrayThe cards loaded inside the visible window — widened by $overscanRows, the same way you page — keyed by their ABSOLUTE index. This is the iteration an owner otherwise hand-rolls as for ($i = $start; $i <= $end; $i++) { $grid->item($i) … }: skeleton indices are simply absent from the result, and the map is ascending.
indicesNeedingPoster(int $overscanRows = 0, ?callable $isFillable = null, ?callable $isCached = null): arrayThe absolute indices inside the visible window that still need a poster, so an owner queues exactly those async fills and nothing else:
columns(): int
visibleRows(): int
totalRows(): int
cellHeight(): int
total(): int
loadedCount(): intHow many loaded cards sit INSIDE the current total. Entries the host spliced past the end of the list (then shrank withTotal) stay in the sparse map for the next widening, but they are not loaded content of this collection — counting them over-reported progress.
cursorIndex(): int
cursorRow(): int
scrollRow(): int
item(int $index): ?PosterCardThe loaded card at an absolute index, or NULL for an index the host has not spliced in yet (a skeleton cell — which is still a hit-testable cell:<index> zone by design, so clicking an unloaded slot works).
cursorCard(): ?PosterCardThe card under the cursor, or NULL when that slot has not been fetched.
positionText(): stringThe grid's own position readout — " (3/12)" in the Rail header's shape, or '' for an empty grid. The grid frame is deliberately chrome-free (every row is cell geometry the owner composes), so unlike Rail it prints no heading: the composing screen places this string where it belongs (before this seam, the 2-D view had no way to tell the user where they were). The bytes come from the one shared positionString() home so grid and rail can never drift apart (sugar-gallery-045).
static positionString(int $oneBased, int $total): stringOne home for the padded (n/total) counter: two-space gutter, one-based position, digits never localised — built here and only here (grid print path and Rail header alike delegate).
fitsViewport(?int $cols = null, ?int $rows = null): boolDoes the configured cell geometry actually fit a viewport? columns() and visibleRows() floor at one, so a sub-cell viewport still renders — and silently LIES about what is visible. This is the detection seam callers want before laying a screen around the grid; the grid keeps its floor rather than collapsing frames to blank. Defaults to the grid's own current viewport.
isEmpty(): bool
static emptyMessage(): stringThe localised empty-state notice (lang key grid.empty) for owners that paint one. render() itself stays silent on an empty grid — it returns '' because no geometry was reserved for a message, and the frame contract (exactly viewport-wide rows or nothing) outranks the nicety; this accessor exists so the sentence is not copy-pasted per app, and it resolves live so a T::setLocale() mid-session is honoured.
render(bool $focused = true, ?ZoneManager $zones = null): stringRender the visible rows. The cell at the cursor is highlighted only when $focused (so an unfocused grid shows no cursor). When a ZoneManager is given, each real cell is wrapped as zone id cell:<index> for mouse hit-testing — the caller scans the assembled frame and resolves clicks.
static clearBoxCache(): intDrop the shared boxed-cell memo, returning how many entries were cleared. The counterpart to PosterCard::clearFitCache(): the cache is self-bounding (BOX_CACHE_CAP), but a long-lived program can call this to reclaim memory eagerly. Purely an optimization — never changes a single rendered byte.

Rail final readonly class

A horizontal carousel of PosterCards with a title, a cursor, and a scroll offset. Immutable; the owning model moves the cursor and swaps in loaded posters. Use a PosterGrid instead when you need a 2-D, virtualized view of a large collection.

MethodSummary
__construct(public string $title, public array $cards = [], int $cursor = 0, int $scroll = 0, public ?array $geometry = null)The main path through the constructor is "restore a saved (cursor, scroll) pair", so the constructor CLAMPS rather than validates: the cursor lands inside [0, count-1] and the scroll at or below it, instead of a stale restore printing e.g. "(1000/2)" with a phantom empty row. Every with*-carrier rides the same clamp via carrying(); the render-time window re-clamp in windowedScroll() still handles perRow changes between moves.
static new(string $title, array $cards = [], int $cursor = 0, int $scroll = 0, ?array $geometry = null): selfCanonical factory — mirrors the public constructor.
withGeometry(int $railWidth, int $cardWidth, int $spacing = 2): selfStore the layout tuple (railWidth, cardWidth, spacing) on the rail so moveCursor() can derive its window without the host re-threading the numbers (sugar-gallery-001). Additive: explicit call-site values always win, and render() keeps taking its own geometry — this stores the same three numbers in ONE place for the zero-arg move path.
withCards(array $cards): selfReplace the card list; the constructor clamp pulls cursor/scroll back into range for the new list. The shared card-map shape law refuses bad maps at this ingress, naming withCards() (sugar-gallery-003).
withCard(PosterCard $card): selfReplace a single card by id (e.g. when its poster finishes loading). A card whose id is not in the list is a silent no-op: the RECEIVER comes back unchanged — the same identity law synced() and withoutItemsOutside() follow; RailTest pins the silent no-op.
withTitle(string $title): selfReturn a copy with a different title (immutable+fluent).
cursorIndex(): intThe cursor position as a method — the grid-shaped read so generic host code can ask any viewport for its position the same way ($grid->cursorIndex() / $rail->cursorIndex()); delegates to the public readonly prop (sugar-gallery-044).
scrollIndex(): intThe first painted row, grid-shaped read; see cursorIndex().
withCursor(int $cursor): selfReturn a copy with a different cursor, clamped to [0, count-1]. Scroll is clamped to at most the cursor so the card stays visible. To restore an arbitrary (cursor, scroll) pair, construct the rail directly: new Rail($title, $cards, $cursor, $scroll) (or new(), same signature) — the constructor applies the SAME clamp, so a stale pair degrades to the nearest legal window rather than rendering lies.
focusedCard(): ?PosterCard
isEmpty(): bool
moveCursor(int $delta, ?int $perRow = null): selfMove the cursor by $delta, scrolling so it stays visible. Omit $perRow to use the stored geometry set by withGeometry(); an explicit $perRow always wins (override). With no stored geometry and no argument, the call fails loud naming both remedies.
static perRow(int $railWidth, int|CardSize $cardWidth, ?int $spacing = null): intHow many cards of $cardWidth fit in $railWidth at $spacing gap. The clamps here are the ONE row-fit law: they mirror the grid's constructor floors (cardWidth ≥ 4) and the rail's render-head clamps, so direct callers and render() can never disagree about the window (each card paints at 4 cells minimum no matter what it is asked for — a perRow computed from an unfloored cardWidth promises more slots than fit).
render(int $railWidth, bool $focused, int|CardSize $cardWidth, ?int $posterHeight = null, ?int $spacing = null): stringPaint the rail: the heading line, then the windowed cards joined at $spacing. The heading is swept by AnsiGuard::stripControls(); the card bodies are NOT swept — if zones mark the same frame, run the rail's output through AnsiGuard::stripSentinels() before composing it (sugar-gallery-033: a forged C1 zone sentinel in un-trusted poster art would otherwise ride the join into the owner's marker scan).
frameHeight(int|CardSize $posterHeight): intLines render() will emit: one head line, the poster block, the title row, plus a progress-bar row when ANY loaded card carries progress. sugar-gallery-026 (G-4 default-leg): the height is reserved from declared geometry instead of measured off a first paint — and Layout::joinHorizontalWithSpacing() pads the uneven blocks to the tallest one, so one bar anywhere raises the whole rail.
